newsitem.title: RWANDA: Ethnic Tutsis accuse Zaire of campaign of genocide.
newsitem.headline: Ethnic Tutsis accuse Zaire of campaign of genocide.

text.p: A group representing ethnic Tutsis living in eastern Zaire on Wednesday accused Zairean soldiers and militiamen of carrying out a campaign of genocide.
Zaire denies all such charges and says its troops are resisting foreign intruders from the east.

A statement issued in the Rwandan capital Kigali by representatives of the Banyamulenge, an established Tutsi community inside Zaire, said eyewitness accounts from those who had fled fighting in the area indicated the "targeting and killing of Banyamulenge throughout eastern Zaire".
It gave no overall estimate for the number of dead, but cited individual villages where it said killings had taken place in the last two months.
The group said that in the villages of Bibogobogo, Bivumu and Magaja in the Fizi zone of eastern Zaire, soldiers and militiamen killed unspecified numbers of people.
"Men, boys and small male children were tied and then thrown into Lake Tanganyika. Women were raped, put into huts and then killed with grenades," it said.
In Kamanyola, where the borders of Zaire, Rwanda and Burundi meet, Hutu militiamen cut off the heads of 41 men and boys and threw them into the Rusizi river, it said.
It alleged many other killings in eastern Zaire which could not be independently verified because of the anarchy prevailing in much of the region.

The Banyamulenge Tutsis, whose uprising against Zairean authorities now threatens to provoke war between Zaire and Tutsi-led neighbour Rwanda, have lived for generations on a high plateau in Zaire's South Kivu.
The Banyamulenge estimate their population there as about 300,000, though some long-time residents in the region believe it is much lower.
